tools.name: compile
tools.title: Compile Omega source
tools.description: Compile Omega (.om) source with the pinned seeded compiler omc (omega-mv@e5b32567). Returns ok, the binary's size and sha256, or the compile error {line, code, meaning, fix}.

source.description: Omega (.om) source text of one unit

tools.name: run
tools.title: Compile and run Omega source
tools.description: Compile Omega source and run the program in an isolated sandbox (no network, no host filesystem, empty environment, CPU/memory/file/process limits). Returns the compile result, capped stdout/stderr and the interpreted exit status (normal, trap N with its meaning, or the limit that stopped it).

source.description: Omega (.om) source text of one unit

stdin.description: bytes given to the program on stdin (default empty)

tools.name: explain_error
tools.title: Explain an Omega error or trap
tools.description: Explain a compile error code 1..30, an `omc: line N: error K` line, `trap T`, or a program exit status 101..114 (trap). Returns meaning, cause, fix, a minimal example and source citations.

query.description: an error code 1..30, an `omc: line N: error K` line, `trap T` (1..14) or an exit status 101..114; a string of 1..200 bytes or a nonnegative integer

tools.name: lookup
tools.title: Look up an Omega word or topic
tools.description: Look up any Omega keyword (all 177 entries of the compiler's keyword table) or a topic (requires, ensures, invariant, result, om2, exit_status, packed_list, paths, host_words, compile_errors, traps, contracts): form, arity, types, result, example and citations. A query that is not an exact keyword or topic searches names and summaries (at most 20 results).

query.description: exact keyword or topic, or a case-insensitive substring to search for

1.cause: The compiler could not read its input (stdin is not readable, e.g. a directory).
1.fix: Give omc a readable source file on stdin.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

1.reproduce: omc < /   (stdin is a directory: the read fails, exit 1, stderr 'omc: line 1: error 1')

2.cause: The compiler could not write the binary (stdout is full or closed).
2.fix: Write omc's stdout to a regular file with space.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

2.reproduce: omc < ok.om > /dev/full   (the write fails with ENOSPC, exit 2)

3.cause: A word is used as a name but nothing of that name is in scope (or a struct has no such field).
3.fix: Declare the name first, or fix its spelling.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

4.cause: The line stops before a required operand or word.
4.fix: Supply the missing operand (see the word's form).

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
error 4 if the line ends before `end`

5.cause: Words remain on the line after a complete statement.
5.fix: Remove the extra words or split the line.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

6.cause: A number has a non-digit character, more than 20 digits or a bad hex form.
6.fix: Write a plain decimal (or OM-2 lowercase 0x hex) number.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
more than 20 digits, or a character that is not a digit, is error 6

7.cause: Two values of an operation, an assignment or a call argument have different types; there are no implicit conversions.
7.fix: Convert explicitly with a type word, e.g. `add int a int b`.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

8.cause: A literal is outside its type, or a count/bound/trap code is out of its range.
8.fix: Use a value inside the type's range or a wider type.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

9.cause: The word is not permitted in this position: break/continue outside a loop, new outside the outermost block, free/own/global/text as a statement, a seventh parameter slot, recursion in function mode.
9.fix: Move the statement to a valid position or use the documented alternative.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

10.cause: A name already in scope, a function or a struct is declared again.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

11.cause: A number appears where no context gives it a type.
11.fix: Prefix it with a type word, e.g. `x = int 5`.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
A bare number takes the type the place needs.

12.cause: More than 16 values are live at once in a function.
12.fix: Split the function or reuse names so fewer values are live.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
A function that needs more than the 16 registers it hands out is error 12.

13.cause: A variable, text, global or constant name has more than 8 characters (functions allow 63).
13.fix: Shorten the name to at most 8 characters.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
Function names may have up to 63 characters; other names up to 8 (error 13).

14.cause: A compiler table is full: too many names/globals, struct fields or cells, break sites, fresh arrays, unroll growth.
14.fix: Reduce the count below the documented capacity.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
Input over a capacity is refused with error 14, never overrun

15.cause: The input ends inside an open block.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

16.cause: A line does not start with a known statement form, or a type/length position holds something else.
16.fix: Check the word's spelling and form with lookup.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
a pool written without its length is refused (error 16)

17.cause: A line follows ret, break, continue, trap or exit in the same block and can never run.
17.fix: Delete the unreachable line or move it before the path end.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
(a later line in the same block is error 17)

18.cause: A function with a result type can reach its end without a ret.
18.fix: Add a ret on every path (or make the function void).

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
A function with a return type whose `end` can be reached is error 18.

19.meaning: global passed or same array twice
19.cause: A global is passed as an argument, or one array is passed twice in a call.
19.fix: Copy the global into a local array (new) or pass distinct arrays.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

20.cause: put, read or an edit argument targets a view or a text.
20.fix: Write into a local, global or edit array instead.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
A view is read-only; `put`, `read` into it, or passing it as edit is error 20.

21.cause: A literal index is outside the array or field.
21.fix: Use an index below the length.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
A number index must be inside A when om4 reads it (error 21)

22.cause: A text literal has an unknown escape or no closing quote.
22.fix: Use only \n \t \\ \" escapes and close the quote.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
any other escape, or a quote missing its end,

23.cause: An array is over 16777216 elements, globals over 1 GiB or local arrays over 4 MiB.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
at most 4 MiB of local arrays (error 23)

24.cause: A conditional branch target is misaligned or more than 2^18 words away.
24.fix: Split very large functions or programs; this is reached only by programs with about 1 MiB of code between a branch and its target.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
else error 24 before any artifact is accepted

24.example_note: No minimal example: it needs about 1 MiB of machine code between a branch and its target.

27.meaning: fresh element read before write (OM-2 init)
27.cause: A fresh parameter element is read before it is definitely written, or the array is passed on.
27.fix: Write every element before reading it (put with a number index).

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
else error 27, `obligation=init`, on the get line

28.cause: seal outside the NAMEmk constructor, or a bad holds predicate.
28.fix: Seal only inside the function named NAME followed by mk.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

29.cause: Layout SIZE outside 1..4096, a field past SIZE or overlapping an earlier field.
29.fix: Keep every field inside SIZE and non-overlapping.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void
SIZE outside 1..4096 or a `layout` after the first `fn` is error 29

30.cause: Misplaced requires/ensures/invariant, result outside a value postcondition, or a forbidden predicate operation.
30.fix: Put contracts first in the function or loop body and use only pure integer/bool operations.

citations.quote: fn fail code ulong to void

1.name: OVERFLOW
1.meaning: checked signed arithmetic out of range
1.cause: Signed add/sub/mul/neg/div/shl produced a value outside the type.
1.fix: Use a wider type, check the range first, or use an unsigned type if wrapping is intended.

citations.quote: Signed add, sub, mul, neg, div and shl trap 1
A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

2.name: DIV0
2.cause: div or rem with a divisor of 0.

citations.quote: div and rem trap 2 when the divisor is 0.
A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

3.name: BOUNDS
3.meaning: index or slice out of bounds
3.cause: A run-time index is not below the length, or a host/read/write slice is outside its array.
3.fix: Check the index against len A, or fix off/n.

citations.quote: traps 3 when it is not below the length
A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

4.name: LOOP_BOUND
4.cause: A while ran more than its bound (default 1000000) iterations.
4.fix: Fix the loop condition or raise bound N (at most 999999).

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

5.name: CAST
5.cause: A conversion `T v` got a value outside T.
5.fix: Check the range before converting, or convert to a wider type.

citations.quote: A conversion `<type> v` traps 5 when the value is outside the new type.
A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

6.name: OOM
6.cause: A call or local array would go below the fixed 8 MiB stack (deep recursion).
6.fix: Bound the recursion or use a loop / smaller local arrays.

citations.quote: a call or a local array that would go below it traps
A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

7.name: SHIFT
7.meaning: shift or rotate amount out of range
7.cause: A shift or rotate amount is outside 0..width-1.
7.fix: Check the amount against the width.

citations.quote: A shift amount outside 0 .. width - 1 traps 7
A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

8.name: RUNTIME
8.cause: A runtime invariant (double release, bad handle) failed; checked native code raises it only through `trap 8`.
8.fix: Find the explicit trap 8 in the program.

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

9.name: REQUIRES
9.cause: A requires clause was false on entry.
9.fix: Call the function only with arguments that satisfy its requires clauses.

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

10.name: ENSURES
10.cause: An ensures, invariant or holds check was false.
10.fix: Fix the function body or loop so the stated property holds.

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

11.name: ARENA_FULL
11.cause: An OSC arena allocation exceeded the arena's capacity; native program mode raises it only through `trap 11`.
11.fix: Find the explicit trap 11 in the program.

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

12.name: STALE
12.cause: A handle whose generation no longer matches its slot; native program mode raises it only through `trap 12`.
12.fix: Find the explicit trap 12 in the program.

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

13.name: POOL_FULL
13.meaning: pool allocation with every slot live
13.cause: An OSC pool allocation found no free slot; native program mode raises it only through `trap 13`.
13.fix: Find the explicit trap 13 in the program.

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code

14.name: RETIRED
14.meaning: pool slot retired at the maximum generation
14.cause: An OSC pool allocation found only retired slots; native program mode raises it only through `trap 14`.
14.fix: Find the explicit trap 14 in the program.

citations.quote: A trap in program mode ends the program with exit status 100 + the trap code
